Combine and transform signed distance functions

Source: R/sdf.R
sdf_blend.Rd

Constructive solid geometry on ggplot3d_sdf shapes (sdf_sphere()). a | b is the union (min(a, b)), a & b the intersection (max(a, b)), a - b removes b from a (max(a, -b)) and -a swaps inside and outside. As in Quilez's catalogue the union is the exact distance outside the shape only, and intersections and differences are lower bounds of the distance.

Usage

sdf_blend(a, b, k = 0.1, mode = c("union", "intersection", "difference"))

sdf_offset(sdf, distance)

sdf_shell(sdf, thickness)

sdf_transform(sdf, translate = c(0, 0, 0), rotate = c(0, 0, 0), scale = 1)

# S3 method for class 'ggplot3d_sdf'
Ops(e1, e2)

Arguments

a, b

Shapes.

k

Blend thickness, in distance units.

mode

"union", "intersection" or "difference" (a without b).

sdf

A shape.

distance

Offset distance.

thickness

Wall thickness.

translate

Translation vector.

rotate

Rotation angles in degrees about x, y and z, applied in that order, or a 3 x 3 rotation matrix.

scale

Positive uniform scale factor.

e1, e2

Shapes.

Value

A ggplot3d_sdf function of x, y and z.

Details

sdf_blend() replaces the minimum (or maximum) by the quadratic polynomial smooth minimum, with k the largest thickness added where the shapes meet, in distance units. sdf_offset() moves the surface outwards by distance (inwards when negative); sdf_shell() keeps a wall of the given thickness centred on the surface. sdf_transform() scales the shape uniformly about the origin, rotates it about the x, y and z axes in turn and then translates it; both keep the distance exact.

Every result records a Lipschitz constant of its value: one for exact distances and their combinations, so the value never exceeds the distance to the surface.

References

Quilez, I. Smooth minimum. https://iquilezles.org/articles/smin/

Quilez, I. Interior SDFs. https://iquilezles.org/articles/interiordistance/

Examples

cut <- sdf_box(size = c(1.6, 1.6, 1.6), radius = 0.1) - sdf_sphere(radius = 1)
blob <- sdf_blend(sdf_sphere(c(-0.5, 0, 0), 0.6), sdf_sphere(c(0.5, 0, 0), 0.6), k = 0.2)
cut
ggplot2::ggplot() +
  geom_isofunction_3d(fun = sdf_shell(blob, 0.1) & sdf_plane(c(0, 1, 0)), n = 20) +
  ggplot2::xlim(-1.3, 1.3) + ggplot2::ylim(-1, 1) +
  scale_z_continuous(limits = c(-1, 1)) + coord_3d()
